summary: Repairs the single fail-open path in v0.7.0. run_contracts_gate warned and returned 0 when contracts.yaml existed but scripts/phasekit-contracts.py did not, so a declaring repo committed with no contract verification at all. It now refuses, routes the failure through the shared record_verify_failure() capture (exit code 5, emitted by the loop rather than by the checker), and names `phasekit upgrade` as the repair so it stays recoverable in one command. PHASEKIT_CONTRACTS_SKIP=1 is checked first and still wins.
suggested_commit_message: v0.7.1: refuse when a declaring repo has no checker
reviewer_notes: Two reasons this was the wrong disposition, both from the addendum and both confirmed in the code: it contradicted the property stated three comment-lines above it (a repo that can edit away the check policing it is not policed), and the realistic trigger is the upgrade seam rather than malice — a project can acquire contracts.yaml from a build while its vendored scripts/ is still pre-v0.7.0, leaving the gate silently off in exactly the window where drift is most likely.

Exit code 5 is deliberately distinct from 2 (malformed declaration). Same reasoning that split 3 from 4 in v0.7.0: the two conditions have different repairs — 2 means fix your file, 5 means upgrade phasekit — and collapsing them sends people to the wrong place. Documented in docs/CONTRACTS.md as loop-emitted, since phasekit-contracts.py's own table stops at 4.

The old pin (test_a_declaration_with_no_checker_warns_rather_than_passing_quietly) asserted only that a WARN substring existed and never inspected the return value, so it passed either way — the addendum called this out and it is exactly why the defect survived review. Replaced with test_a_declaration_with_no_checker_refuses_and_names_the_repair, which asserts the DISPOSITION (return 1, no return 0 on that branch, names the repair, flows through the shared capture) rather than the wording.

A structural pin alone is what let this slip, so the repair also ships a functional pin: test_a_declaring_repo_with_no_checker_cannot_commit drives the real loop with the checker deleted and asserts no commit lands. Both new pins were verified to FAIL against the v0.7.0 script and pass against the fix (script reverted in isolation via git stash, tests kept) — they are not vacuous.

Two guardrails on the new refusal, both pinned: it keys off the DECLARATION and not the missing file, so every pre-v0.7.0 project without a contracts.yaml is unaffected (otherwise this patch would stop the entire fleet committing); and the operator hatch still wins, which is what makes refusing safe rather than wedging.

deferred_items.description: Upgrade resting projects to v0.7.1 (self-update, then per-project upgrade + check). Partial is harmless: the mechanism is inert until a repo writes contracts.yaml, and none has one.

commands_run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'  -> 256 tests OK
git stash push -- scripts/run-until-done.sh && python3 -m unittest tests.test_contracts_gate_v070  -> 2 FAILURES (the new pins), confirming they are not vacuous
python3 scripts/enrich-project.py --self-check  -> 116 tracked files, 0 unclassified, 0 double-classified
smoke: a declaring repo with no checker refuses, does not commit, and writes phase-verify-failed.json with exit_code 5 / label contracts / command 'phasekit upgrade'
verification.acceptance_criteria_met: the one fail-open path in v0.7.0 now fails closed, recoverably; the weak pin that let it through is replaced by one that asserts the disposition, backed by an end-to-end pin
